title: Incident category → Support/CS escalation playbook (Taxonomy v1)
author: Dev Patel
body:
## Purpose
This playbook helps Support and Customer Success (CS) respond consistently when production issues occur, using **Incident Taxonomy v1** categories.

It covers:
- What to tell customers (message framing + required info)
- What ETAs we can commit to (first response + next update cadence)
- **When and how to page Engineering/SRE** based on category and severity

This is a Support-facing operational guide. Security incidents follow the Security IR process; Support should still use the shared metadata fields (customer, region, surface) but must not run comms independently.

---

## Scope
**In scope:** Hosted API, Dedicated GPU pools, and Private deployments where Redwood is the primary operator for day-2 ops.

**Out of scope:** Customer-managed on-prem incidents where Redwood is advisory-only (use the “Private (customer-operated)” handling guidance below).

---

## Roles and escalation channels (default)
- **Support on-call (SOC):** owns customer triage, ticket updates, and internal escalations.
- **CSM/AM:** owns executive alignment for enterprise accounts and coordinates comms with customer stakeholders.
- **Incident Commander (IC):** SRE, once a Sev1/Sev2 incident is declared.

### Slack channels
- #support (Support triage + coordination)
- #incidents (active incident comms + IC updates)
- #eng-oncall (engineering on-call coordination)
- #statuspage (internal status page coordination)

### Paging shortcuts (use PagerDuty / on-call tool)
- **SRE On-call:** page for Sev1 always; Sev2 if multi-customer or >15 min unresolved.
- **Platform On-call (Routing/Control Plane):** routing/policy/control-plane categories.
- **Infra/Fleet On-call:** capacity/fleet/network categories.
- **Runtime On-call:** runtime crash/scheduler/model instability categories.

If unsure, page **SRE On-call** first and include suspected category + impacted surface.

---

## Support triage checklist (first 5 minutes)
Collect these fields before paging whenever possible (don’t delay paging for Sev1):
1) **Customer/org name** + contract tier (Enterprise/Dedicated/Standard)
2) **Deployment mode:** Hosted / Dedicated / Private
3) **Region(s):** e.g., us-east-1, eu-west-1
4) **Impacted surface:** API (chat/completions/embeddings), streaming, console, webhooks
5) **Symptoms:** 5xx, timeouts, elevated latency, disconnects, auth failures, incorrect outputs
6) **Start time (UTC)** + last known good time
7) **Example request IDs / trace IDs** (minimum 3) and timestamps
8) **Model + version** (if applicable) + endpoint route
9) **Observed scope:** single customer vs multiple; specific region or global

Create or update the internal incident record when:
- ≥2 customers report similar symptoms within 10 minutes, OR
- One enterprise/dedicated customer has a hard outage, OR
- Any issue appears “systemic” (routing, fleet, widespread 5xx/timeout).

---

## Communication rules of thumb
### What we can say early (safe language)
- Confirm we are investigating; describe **symptoms** (timeouts, elevated error rates) rather than root cause.
- If impacted surface and region are known, include them.
- Set clear expectations for next update time.

### What we should avoid early
- Do not claim a root cause until IC/owning team confirms.
- Do not give precise restoration times unless IC provides an ETA.
- Do not promise credits/penalties; route to CS leadership.

### Update cadence (customer-facing)
- **Sev1:** first update within **15 minutes**, then every **30 minutes** (or sooner on major changes)
- **Sev2:** first update within **30 minutes**, then every **60 minutes**
- **Sev3:** first update within **1 business day** (or faster for enterprise), then as agreed

For enterprise customers, follow account comms plan with CSM/AM; still adhere to the cadence above.

---

## Category → Support guidance + escalation triggers
Use the table below to map the incident category to:
- Customer messaging guidance (what to ask for / what to tell)
- Typical mitigation patterns (helps Support interpret updates)
- When to page Eng/SRE

> Note: categories are designed to be chosen quickly during live response. If the category changes post-incident, Support should update the ticket and customer narrative ("initially suspected X, confirmed Y").

### A) Routing / Control plane / Policy
| Taxonomy category | Common customer symptoms | What Support should ask for | What Support can say (early) | When to page (minimum) | Expected mitigation pattern |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Routing / smart-router degradation** | Elevated 5xx/timeouts, wrong region routing, sudden latency spikes across multiple models | Request IDs, region, endpoint route, whether failures cluster by model, timestamps | “We’re investigating an issue affecting request routing in <region/s>. Next update by <time>.” | Page **SRE + Platform On-call** immediately if >1 customer or enterprise impact | Traffic shift to healthy pools/regions; enable fallback policy; temporarily restrict high-cost routes |
| **Control plane (config/rollouts/policy) regression** | Failures after deploy; feature flags misapplied; sudden auth/limits behavior changes | When did issue start; any recent config changes on customer side; endpoint + org ID | “We’re investigating a control-plane issue affecting policy/config application. We’ll provide updates as changes roll out.” | Page **Platform On-call**; page **SRE** if customer-impacting for >15 min | Rollback/revert config; disable flag; redeploy control plane; invalidate caches |
| **Quota / rate-limit misbehavior (platform-side)** | Unexpected 429s, incorrect quota enforcement, tier misapplied | Org ID, headers, rate-limit response details | “We’re checking rate limiting/quota enforcement for your org. Next update by <time>.” | Page **Platform On-call** if widespread or enterprise; otherwise triage with platform SME | Hotfix policy; restore correct quota record; temporary overrides |

### B) Capacity / Fleet / Networking
| Taxonomy category | Common customer symptoms | What Support should ask for | What Support can say (early) | When to page (minimum) | Expected mitigation pattern |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Capacity exhaustion (dedicated pool or hosted regional capacity)** | Timeouts, queueing, increased latency at peak, 503/529 style overload | Region, time window, concurrency patterns, whether streaming worsens | “We’re seeing elevated load/capacity pressure in <region/pool>. We’re working to restore performance.” | Page **Infra/Fleet On-call**; page **SRE** if enterprise/dedicated or multi-customer | Add capacity; adjust autoscaling; shed load; enforce backpressure; reroute |
| **Autoscaling policy failure** | Sustained saturation despite expected scale-out; recurring during predictable peaks | Pool name, region, start time, request rate if known | “We’re investigating autoscaling behavior for <pool/region>. Next update by <time>.” | Page **Infra/Fleet On-call**; **SRE** if impact >15 min | Fix scaling signals; manual scale; adjust min/max; patch scheduler inputs |
| **Fleet provisioning / GPU node health** | Sudden capacity drop; increased errors in one AZ; repeated retries | Region/AZ (if known), time window, whether issue is single model or all | “We’re investigating infrastructure health in <region>. We’ll update after mitigation steps.” | Page **Infra/Fleet On-call** immediately for systemic signals | Drain unhealthy nodes; replace nodes; failover AZ; re-balance pools |
| **Network (internal) / DNS / edge connectivity** | High timeouts, TLS handshake errors, regional reachability issues, packet loss | Customer ASN/ISP if known, traceroutes (if enterprise can provide), region | “We’re investigating connectivity issues affecting <region>. Mitigation may include routing traffic via alternate paths/regions.” | Page **Infra/Network On-call + SRE** immediately if widespread | Traffic engineering; move traffic to alternate POP/region; provider escalation |

### C) Runtime / Model serving
| Taxonomy category | Common customer symptoms | What Support should ask for | What Support can say (early) | When to page (minimum) | Expected mitigation pattern |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Runtime crash / OOM / server instability** | Sudden 5xx spikes, requests failing mid-stream, “internal error” | Request IDs, model, max tokens, context length, streaming vs non-streaming | “We’re investigating runtime instability impacting <model/region>. Next update by <time>.” | Page **Runtime On-call + SRE** if multi-customer or enterprise | Rollback runtime version; adjust memory/batching; drain pods; restart workers |
| **Scheduler / batching regression** | Latency increases without corresponding error spikes; p95/p99 blowups under load | Model, region, request sizes, concurrency; examples around p99 | “We’re investigating performance degradation for <model/region>. Mitigation may include traffic shaping.” | Page **Runtime On-call** if sustained >15 min or enterprise | Reduce batch size; disable experimental scheduler; adjust queue priorities |
| **Model-specific instability (weights/tokenizer/quant profile)** | Failures isolated to one model; quality regressions; unexpected output format breaks | Model version, prompt examples (sanitized), output diffs, start time | “We’re investigating an issue isolated to <model>. As mitigation we may route to a compatible variant.” | Page **Runtime On-call**; include model/version | Rollback model version; route to stable variant; disable quant profile |
| **Streaming path errors (gateway/runtime boundary)** | Stream disconnects, partial responses, client receives EOF | Client SDK version, transport (SSE/WebSocket), timeouts, request IDs | “We’re investigating streaming reliability impacting some requests. We’ll share workarounds if available.” | Page **Platform or Runtime** based on signals; if unsure page **SRE** | Adjust gateway limits; fix keepalive; tune buffering; roll back edge change |

### D) API gateway / auth / billing
| Taxonomy category | Common customer symptoms | What Support should ask for | What Support can say (early) | When to page (minimum) | Expected mitigation pattern |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Auth / API key validation / IAM integration** | 401/403 spikes, “invalid key” for valid keys, KMS-related errors (Private) | Org ID, key last rotated, request IDs, whether new keys affected | “We’re investigating authentication issues affecting API access. Next update by <time>.” | Page **Platform On-call**; page **SRE** if widespread | Rollback auth deploy; fix key cache; restore IAM integration; rotate signing keys |
| **Billing / metering / usage reporting (customer-visible)** | Incorrect usage spikes, missing usage, limits triggered incorrectly | Org ID, dashboard screenshots (if allowed), time window | “We’re investigating usage reporting/metering. Core inference may be unaffected; we’ll confirm shortly.” | Page **Platform On-call** if enterprise or limits are impacted | Backfill usage; correct metering pipeline; apply temporary limit overrides |
| **API gateway / request parsing / edge limits** | 413/431/502 errors, header size issues, sudden request rejection | Payload sizes, headers, SDK version, request IDs | “We’re investigating API gateway behavior affecting request acceptance. We’ll update with mitigation/workarounds.” | Page **Platform On-call**; **SRE** if widespread | Roll back gateway config; adjust limits; hotfix parsing |

### E) Observability / tooling (customer-facing)
| Taxonomy category | Common customer symptoms | What Support should ask for | What Support can say (early) | When to page (minimum) | Expected mitigation pattern |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Console degradation (dashboards/usage latency)** | Console down/slow; usage charts delayed; logs missing | Org ID, impacted console pages, screenshots, time window | “We’re investigating an issue affecting the Console. Inference may be unaffected; we’ll confirm.” | Page **Observability On-call** if enterprise or widespread | Fix frontend/API; backfill data; route to fallback data source |
| **Status page / incident comms pipeline issue** | Status page not updating; webhook alerts not delivered | What event failed, timestamps | “We’re investigating an issue with our comms pipeline. We’ll provide updates via email/ticket as needed.” | Page **SRE** (comms integrity is Sev2+) | Manual comms; restore status tooling; validate subscribers |

---

## Dedicated and Private nuances
### Dedicated (reserved capacity)
Treat these as **higher urgency** because of contractual expectations and single-customer blast radius:
- If a Dedicated customer reports sustained saturation or hard outage: page **Infra/Fleet On-call + SRE** immediately, even if only one account.
- Always capture: **pool name**, **commit level**, and whether **burst capacity** is enabled.

Message framing:
- Avoid language implying “shared capacity” for Dedicated.
- Prefer: “We’re investigating your dedicated pool health/capacity and working to restore expected throughput.”

### Private (Redwood-operated day-2)
- Page the **Private on-call / SRE** route (if configured) when the issue impacts customer production.
- Capture: customer environment name, region/VPC, version of Redwood Private, last successful deploy time.

### Private (customer-operated / on-prem)
- If Redwood is advisory-only, do not declare a Redwood Sev1 unless the issue is traced to Redwood-managed services.
- Support actions:
  1) Ask for customer logs/metrics bundle per the Private support package.
  2) Engage Solutions Engineering / Private SME during business hours unless production outage and enterprise.

---

## Paging decision policy (Support quick matrix)
Support should page according to **impact** + **time** + **confidence**.

### Always page immediately
- **Any Sev1** symptom (hard outage, widespread 5xx, or enterprise/dedicated down)
- Multi-customer reports with consistent symptoms within 10 minutes
- Suspected routing, fleet, or network incident

### Page within 15 minutes if unresolved
- Sev2 performance degradation (p95/p99 latency) affecting production usage
- Recurring stream disconnects affecting multiple customers
- Console outage for enterprise accounts

### Don’t page (yet); continue triage
- Single customer integration issues without systemic signals
- Known maintenance windows with communicated impact
- Issues confined to customer code/SDK misconfiguration (but still help the customer)

If uncertain after 10 minutes, page **SRE On-call** with:
- suspected taxonomy category
- scope (customers/regions)
- evidence (request IDs, graphs if available)

---

## Customer messaging templates
### Initial acknowledgement (Sev1)
“Thanks for flagging this. We’re actively investigating an issue affecting <symptom> in <region/surface>. We’ll share the next update by <UTC time> (within 15 minutes). If you can share 2–3 example request IDs and timestamps, that will help us correlate quickly.”

### Performance degradation (Sev2)
“We’re investigating elevated latency affecting <model/endpoint> in <region>. We’ll provide an update by <UTC time> and continue updates at least hourly until resolved. If possible, please share example request IDs and approximate concurrency when the slowdown occurs.”

### Dedicated capacity saturation
“We’re investigating capacity pressure in your dedicated pool (<pool name>/<region>) that is impacting throughput/latency. We’re working on mitigation steps now (e.g., scaling/rebalancing) and will provide the next update by <UTC time>.”

### Streaming disconnects workaround (only if validated by Eng)
“We’re investigating streaming disconnects. As a temporary workaround, you can switch to non-streaming responses / increase client-side read timeout to <value>. We’ll confirm when the underlying issue is fully resolved.”

### Post-resolution note
“Service is restored as of <UTC time>. We’re completing follow-up analysis to prevent recurrence. We’ll share a summary when available; for enterprise accounts, we can also schedule an incident review.”

---

## What Support should include when escalating internally
Paste this block into #incidents or the escalation ticket:
- Customer/org:
- Tier (Enterprise/Dedicated/Standard):
- Deployment (Hosted/Dedicated/Private):
- Region(s):
- Surface (chat/completions/embeddings/streaming/console):
- Suspected taxonomy category:
- Severity (if known):
- Start time (UTC):
- Current impact (5xx %, latency, disconnect rate):
- Example request IDs (3+) + timestamps:
- Any recent change correlation (deploy/config/traffic spike):

---

## FAQ / common edge cases
### “Is it routing overload or capacity exhaustion?”
Use this heuristic:
- **Capacity exhaustion**: queueing/saturation within a pool; often limited to a region/pool; mitigation is scale/add GPUs.
- **Routing degradation**: misrouting, incorrect fallback policy, traffic steering issues; mitigation is route policy/traffic shifting.

If unclear, choose **Routing / smart-router degradation** initially and note “suspected capacity component,” then page SRE.

### “One customer only, but they’re enterprise.”
Treat as incident-level urgency if production is impacted. Dedicated and enterprise hosted customers can be Sev1 even with single-account scope.

### “Customer asks for SLA credit.”
Do not commit. Route to **CS leadership (Rachel Kim)** and capture timeline + evidence. Support can state: “We will review impact against contractual terms after the incident is resolved.”
